guitar.modelsText: Gibson SG / Fender Telecaster / Gibson Les Paul
guitar.notes: Confirmed — Louis Bertignac is well known in French rock for SG and Telecaster usage; medium confidence appropriate given two guitarists and varied gear.

tone.target: jangly chorus clean with light delay and edge-of-breakup crunch
tone.profile: jangly chorus clean with light delay and edge-of-breakup crunch
tone.summary: A shimmering, jangly sound built around a Fender-style clean amp (US Deluxe) combined with Chorus for shimmer and a subtle boost/OD for controlled edge-of-breakup grit.

rig.name: Téléphone - Un Autre Monde - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide subtle lift and controlled edge-of-breakup grit on peaks.
blocks.gap: Using Boost for gentle saturation rather than a dedicated OD pedal, matching the 'light grit' requirement.

alternatives.reason: A more classic clean boost option.

blocks.purpose: Create the required 'chorus shimmer' and jangly texture.
Bypass or use a very subtle drive if needed (kept off to maintain clean focus).
blocks.gap: The Boost pedal handles the required light grit; dedicated distortion is avoided.

blocks.purpose: Provide the bright, clean, Fender/Vox-style foundation.
Match the clean, bright sound and single-coil vibe (Fender/Vox combo).
Enhance the bright attack and jangly high-end frequencies.
blocks.gap: Used to fine-tune the brightness required for 'jangly' tones.

blocks.purpose: Implement the required 'short delay' for shimmer and space.
Add subtle space and depth without muddying the clean tone.
blocks.gap: Room reverb is ideal for maintaining clarity in a jangly context.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and tonal depth for a more authentic jangly clean tone.

proposals.reason: Enhance the vintage, bright single-coil sound and add depth to the clean tone.
